prerequisites: Basic knowledge of vector calculus, integral and differential calculus

learning_outcomes.text: Students should first learn vector calculus to independently calculate angles, lengths, areas, volumes, orientations, and parameterizations of lines and surfaces in geometry.

They should be able to calculate arbitrary, statically determinate rigid bodies to analytically and numerically determine bearing reactions, joint forces, and internal forces using the free-body diagram method. This is associated with a fundamental understanding of forces, moments, and distributed loads.
Furthermore, they can identify, calculate, and distinguish different "center of gravity concepts" for composite bodies (lines, areas, volumes).

In addition, the student knows the difference between static, kinetic, and cable friction and can calculate or graphically determine the upper limits for statically determinate friction problems. Students acquire purely technical competencies from the fundamentals of rigid body mechanics.

syllabus_topics: Center of mass, line, area and volume centroid
Internal loads in rods and beams
Static and kinetic friction as well as cable friction
